name: Google Shape;17;p3
text:
Customer Service
Agent Induction

name: Google Shape;18;p3
text: A clear, supportive introduction to Q and the way we care for customers.

name: Google Shape;19;p3
text: Q Intelligence

Discussion points:
• Welcome agents and explain how their work supports a respectful, reliable customer experience.
• Set expectations for participation, questions and asking for help.

Activity:
• Pair introductions: each person shares one service quality they value as a customer and one behavior that demonstrates it. Invite a few examples; no personal wellbeing disclosures are needed.

name: Google Shape;28;p4
text: What is Q?

name: Google Shape;29;p4
text: An AI-powered wellbeing and personal growth platform for LGBTQ+ people and allies.

name: Google Shape;30;p4
text:
Technology and wellbeing tools in one secure platform
Guided support, mood tracking and journaling
Resources for reflection and personal growth

name: Google Shape;31;p4
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Describe Q as a secure platform combining technology, wellbeing tools, guided support and personal growth resources.
• Explain the visible features listed here: mood tracking, journaling, guided support and reflection resources. Avoid promising clinical outcomes or features not shown in approved guidance.

Activity:
• In pairs, give a 30-second plain-language explanation of Q to a new user. Partners identify one clear phrase and one point that needs approved guidance.

name: Google Shape;40;p5
text: Q’s mission and values

name: Google Shape;41;p5
text: Support people as they understand themselves and make changes that feel right for them.

name: Google Shape;42;p5
text:
Build positive habits at the person’s own pace
Make support available when it is needed
Put trust, privacy and user wellbeing at the centre

name: Google Shape;43;p5
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Connect personal pace, access to support, trust, privacy and wellbeing to everyday service choices.
• Invite agents to consider how an interaction can respect a customer’s own goals without directing or judging them.

Activity:
• For each value on the slide, ask pairs to name one observable support behaviour that would demonstrate it. Share one example per pair.

name: Google Shape;52;p6
text: Induction at a glance

name: Google Shape;53;p6
text: A day of practical learning, guided practice and support.

name: Google Shape;54;p6
text:
Morning: role boundaries, data protection and escalation
Afternoon: Q tour, Microsoft 365 and CRM practice
Finish: case simulations, assessment and sign-off

name: Google Shape;55;p6
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Walk through the morning, afternoon and finish, showing how the topics build from safe principles to practice.
• Explain that practice and sign-off are opportunities to identify support needs, not a reason to guess when uncertain.

Activity:
• Ask each learner to choose one topic they feel confident about and one they want to practise. Capture the latter for coaching later in the day.

name: Google Shape;64;p7
text: Roles and boundaries

name: Google Shape;65;p7
text: Our role is to make each support interaction clear, respectful and useful.

name: Google Shape;66;p7
text:
Listen carefully and respond without judgement
Explain Q features using current approved guidance
Stay within your training, access and authority

name: Google Shape;67;p7
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Emphasise listening, non-judgement, accurate approved information and staying within training and access.
• Distinguish helpful service from counselling, diagnosis, personal opinions or making commitments outside authority.

Activity:
• Read three short statements aloud: “I can show you where to find that setting”; “It sounds like you have depression”; “I’ll guarantee this is fixed today.” Learners classify as in role or out of role and rewrite the out-of-role replies safely.

name: Google Shape;76;p8
text: When to pause and escalate

name: Google Shape;77;p8
text: A safe hand-off is part of good customer service.

name: Google Shape;78;p8
text:
Pause when identity, access or the correct next step is uncertain
Escalate privacy, security, safety or legal concerns promptly
Do not diagnose, counsel, make legal decisions or promise outcomes

name: Google Shape;79;p8
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• A pause is appropriate when identity, access, risk or the correct next step is unclear.
• Escalation protects the customer and agent; use the designated route and share only relevant facts. Do not promise an outcome or investigate beyond authority.

Activity:
• Scenario sort: learners label each case “continue”, “pause and check” or “escalate”: uncertain account identity; request for a feature walkthrough; report of a security concern; question asking for a legal interpretation. Discuss the route specified by local procedure.

name: Google Shape;88;p9
text: Legal awareness and data protection

name: Google Shape;89;p9
text: Handle information with care, for a clear support purpose.

name: Google Shape;90;p9
text:
Use and record only what is needed for the enquiry
Keep notes accurate, factual and respectful
Use approved systems and follow the organisation’s procedures
Route legal or privacy questions to the designated contact

name: Google Shape;91;p9
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Use information only for a clear support purpose and only what is needed.
• Keep records factual, respectful and in approved systems; route rights or legal questions to the designated contact rather than deciding them.

Activity:
• Show a fictional over-detailed case note. Ask learners to remove irrelevant personal details and rewrite it as a concise, factual record. Discuss what should be routed instead of answered directly.

name: Google Shape;100;p10
text: Everyday information safety

name: Google Shape;101;p10
text: Small checks help protect customer trust.

name: Google Shape;102;p10
text:
Never request passwords, one-time codes or reset links
Do not request journals, mood logs or private chat screenshots
Check recipients, attachments and quoted history before sending
Do not move customer information to personal tools or storage

name: Google Shape;103;p10
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Reinforce never requesting passwords, one-time codes, reset links, journals, mood logs or private-chat screenshots.
• Check recipient, attachments and quoted history before sending; keep customer information in approved tools.

Activity:
• “Spot the risk” email review: provide a fictional message containing a wrong recipient, unnecessary screenshot and quoted customer history. Learners identify each risk and state the safe correction before sending.

title: Security incidents, rights requests and escalation

name: Google Shape;112;p11
text: Security incidents, rights requests and escalation

name: Google Shape;113;p11
text: Recognise the concern, protect the information and route it.

name: Google Shape;114;p11
text:
If information is misdirected or exposed, stop copying or forwarding it
Report suspected incidents promptly through the approved route
Record only the minimum facts needed for the report
Route rights requests and authority demands securely; do not disclose data yourself

name: Google Shape;115;p11
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Treat suspected disclosure, account compromise or unusual access as a concern to report promptly through the designated incident route.
• Recognise a rights request even when phrased informally; acknowledge it and route it to the designated privacy contact. Do not delete, export or promise a deadline unless procedure authorises it.

Activity:
• In triads, role-play an agent receiving (1) a suspected account compromise and (2) a request to see or erase personal information. Practise acknowledging, recording only necessary facts and routing without making a determination.

name: Google Shape;124;p12
text: Q platform tour

name: Google Shape;125;p12
text: Explore the customer-facing experience with a demo account or current published guidance.

name: Google Shape;126;p12
text:
Account creation, sign-in and password recovery
Q Chat and available AI modes
Mood tracking, journaling and guided programmes
Memory features, user settings and help routes

name: Google Shape;127;p12
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Demonstrate the platform areas named in the approved environment: mood tracking, journaling, guided programmes, memory features and user settings.
• Explain that agents should guide navigation, not inspect or request private wellbeing content. Confirm any uncertain feature details against current guidance.

Activity:
• Give learners a guided “find the setting” task in a training or demo account. Ask them to describe the navigation steps without opening or discussing personal entries.

name: Google Shape;136;p13
text: Explaining features safely

name: Google Shape;137;p13
text: Describe what a feature does while respecting what remains private.

name: Google Shape;138;p13
text:
Show where customers find the feature
Use current Help content for steps and limitations
Explain what support can verify and when to escalate
Never inspect private entries or ask customers to share them

name: Google Shape;139;p13
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Describe what a feature does in neutral, plain language and explain its limits using approved wording.
• Do not interpret mood entries, infer diagnoses or claim that a feature will produce a particular wellbeing result.

Activity:
• Learners rewrite two overclaims into safe explanations: “This will cure your anxiety” and “I can tell from your mood log what is wrong.” Ask them to keep the explanation useful and non-clinical.

name: Google Shape;148;p14
text: Support boundaries in practice

name: Google Shape;149;p14
text: Warm support can be direct and careful at the same time.

name: Google Shape;150;p14
text:
Acknowledge the customer’s concern without defending AI output
Ask only for the non-sensitive details needed to understand the issue
Do not offer clinical advice or guarantee a product outcome
Q is not an emergency service; use approved crisis guidance for immediate danger

name: Google Shape;151;p14
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Warmth and empathy can coexist with clear professional boundaries.
• Acknowledge feelings without probing for intimate details; offer an appropriate platform or support route and escalate concerns using procedure.

Activity:
• Role-play a customer asking the agent to interpret a journal entry. Practise a brief empathic boundary statement and an appropriate next step; observer gives feedback on tone and scope.

name: Google Shape;162;p15
text: Microsoft 365 and Outlook

name: Google Shape;163;p15
text: Use your own organisation account and approved communication tools.

name: Google Shape;164;p15
text:
Sign in using your individual account and required security checks
Use Outlook search, folders, replies, calendar and approved templates
Verify recipient, attachment and quoted content before sending
Report suspicious messages through the approved process

name: Google Shape;165;p15
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Identify the approved communication tools and the organisation’s expectations for account security and professional messages.
• Check recipients, attachments, links and quoted history; use the correct account and approved storage locations.

Activity:
• Using a training mailbox, learners draft a short acknowledgement, then run a pre-send check aloud: recipient, purpose, minimum necessary content, attachment and quoted history.

name: Google Shape;174;p16
text: Shared mailbox and My inbox

name: Google Shape;175;p16
text: Choose the right work identity and stay within granted access.

name: Google Shape;176;p16
text:
Use the shared mailbox for the team’s customer-service identity
Use My inbox only for authorised work in your own mailbox
A visible mailbox is not permission to browse unrelated messages
Keep customer information in approved channels

name: Google Shape;177;p16
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Explain the difference between shared team work and an agent’s assigned/personal work queue as defined by local setup.
• Make ownership visible: avoid duplicate replies, check assignment/status and leave a clear handover when work moves.

Activity:
• Simulate two agents seeing the same enquiry. Learners agree who owns the reply, update the practice status and write a concise internal handover.

name: Google Shape;186;p17
text: Customer records, tickets and activities (CRM)

name: Google Shape;187;p17
text: Accurate records help the next person continue the support journey.

name: Google Shape;188;p17
text:
Sign in with your own account and follow your role permissions
Search with the minimum approved identifiers; verify identity as required
Create or update tickets with a clear subject, category, status and owner
Link communications and record the next action in the approved fields

name: Google Shape;189;p17
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Capture accurate identifiers and only information needed to resolve or route the enquiry.
• Keep status, owner and activity history current; distinguish customer-visible replies from internal notes.

Activity:
• From a fictional enquiry, learners create a practice record and ticket with a clear subject, concise factual summary, appropriate category/owner and next action. Review for unnecessary sensitive detail.

name: Google Shape;198;p18
text: CRM notes, hand-offs and closure

name: Google Shape;199;p18
text: Record what the next person needs to know—nothing more.

name: Google Shape;200;p18
text:
Write concise, objective notes; separate verified facts from customer statements
Keep highly sensitive Q content out of notes unless an approved process requires it
Assign and hand off with a clear owner and next action
Correct mistakes through the authorised process; preserve record history

name: Google Shape;201;p18
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• A useful note lets the next agent understand what happened, what was checked, what remains and who owns the next step.
• Close only when the applicable process says the request is complete; avoid unexplained closure or unsupported claims.

Activity:
• Give pairs a messy fictional case history. They produce a four-part handover: issue, actions taken, current status, next owner/action. Another pair checks if it is factual and sufficient.

name: Google Shape;210;p19
text: The customer support journey

name: Google Shape;211;p19
text: Keep the customer informed while moving the request through the right route.

name: Google Shape;212;p19
text:
Help customers find the appropriate signed-in or guest request route
Review, assign and respond to requests using the support workflow
Use public replies for customers and internal notes for staff
Check the sent record before retrying an uncertain notification

name: Google Shape;213;p19
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Walk through the route from finding the support channel to triage, response, hand-off and follow-up.
• Keep the customer informed using confirmed information; check the sent record before retrying if a notification’s status is uncertain.

Activity:
• Sequence shuffled workflow cards into the correct local support journey. At each hand-off, learners identify what the customer should be told and what belongs in an internal note.

name: Google Shape;222;p20
text: Clear, professional written responses

name: Google Shape;223;p20
text: Each reply should make the next step easy to understand.

name: Google Shape;224;p20
text:
Acknowledge the question and clarify the product issue
Give one useful next step based on current approved guidance
Use templates as drafts and check each detail before sending
Avoid invented timelines, delivery claims and unsupported promises

name: Google Shape;225;p20
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• A good reply acknowledges the question, gives a clear supported next step and uses a respectful tone.
• Templates are drafts: verify names, details, links and relevance. Avoid invented timelines, guarantees and unsupported claims.

Activity:
• Rewrite a vague or overly certain response into three parts: acknowledgement, one confirmed next step, and a realistic closing that does not promise an outcome.

name: Google Shape;234;p21
text: Integrated case simulations

name: Google Shape;235;p21
text: Practise the complete workflow using fictional customer details.

name: Google Shape;236;p21
text:
Read the enquiry and identify the customer’s actual need
Draft an empathetic response using approved guidance
Update the practice CRM record with only necessary facts
Assign or escalate the case and explain the next step

name: Google Shape;237;p21
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Explain that the simulation combines listening, feature guidance, privacy, records, written communication and escalation.
• Use fictional details only; learners should pause and consult guidance whenever facts or authority are unclear.

Activity:
• Run a small-group case: customer asks about a Q feature, includes sensitive journal content, and reports difficulty accessing an account. Assign agent, customer and observer roles; rotate and debrief the safe next steps.

name: Google Shape;246;p22
text: Observed assessment

name: Google Shape;247;p22
text: Show safe, accurate work from first contact through hand-off.

name: Google Shape;248;p22
text:
Privacy and minimum-information handling
Q feature explanations and professional boundaries
Correct mailbox choice and safe message checks
CRM accuracy, escalation judgement and clear communication

name: Google Shape;249;p22
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Describe the observable criteria: minimum-information handling, accurate explanations, professional boundaries, correct tool use, sound escalation and clear communication.
• Feedback should identify evidence, a specific improvement and a chance to practise again. Follow the organisation’s sign-off process.

Activity:
• Learner completes one short fictional case while trainer observes with the listed criteria. Give one strength and one specific practice point; allow a second attempt where needed.

name: Google Shape;258;p23
text: Knowledge check, coaching and sign-off

name: Google Shape;259;p23
text: A short check plus observed practice confirms readiness.

name: Google Shape;260;p23
text:
Complete a knowledge check on Q, privacy, tools and escalation
Review individual feedback and practise any missed steps
Confirm accounts, permissions and local procedures are ready
Begin live work after the authorised supervisor signs off

name: Google Shape;261;p23
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Check understanding of Q, privacy, tools, boundaries and escalation, then address gaps through coaching.
• Confirm accounts, permissions and local procedures with the authorised supervisor; sign-off follows the stated process before live work.

Activity:
• Use a brief verbal round: “What would make you pause?”, “What must never be requested?”, “Where does a rights request go?” Learner identifies one next coaching goal and any unanswered question.

name: Google Shape;270;p24
text: Welcome to the team

name: Google Shape;271;p24
text: Every interaction is a chance to offer clear, affirming support.

name: Google Shape;272;p24
text:
Stay curious. Protect privacy. Ask for help when unsure.
Q Intelligence · Customer Service Agent Induction

name: Google Shape;273;p24
text: Q Intelligence · Customer Service Induction

Discussion points:
• Close by reinforcing curiosity, privacy and asking for help when unsure.
• Invite final questions and explain where agents can find current guidance and supervisor support.

Activity:
• Each learner completes an exit ticket: one safe practice they will use, one escalation route they will remember, and one question or coaching need. Thank the group and confirm the next step in onboarding.
